audit.why: 50.72% over 901 games — the largest sample in this slice and a true coin-flip. diff EVEN / 6.0 and carry threat 8.5 are right: Sylas owns levels 2-3, Cho'Gath owns 6, and the game is decided by who snowballed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven stages contradict the page's own whys[] and its own early prose. whys[1] says 'Sylas owns level 2' and whys[2] says 'it stays his', yet both stages are scored Cho'Gath — while the early paragraph opens 'Sylas owns levels 2-3 here'. whys[4] says 'Feast at 6 is your spike' but Level 6 is scored Skill. whys[5] says 'it reads even' and whys[6] says 'a coinflip', yet First item and 2+ items are both scored Cho'Gath.
audit.why: The packet chart matches the whys and the prose row for row. Mechanically: at 2-3 Sylas has a 775-range Chain Lash, a 400-range dash, and Kingslayer refunding the trade, against a Cho'Gath whose only tool is a delayed ground-pop. At 6 Feast is a true-damage execute Kingslayer cannot heal back. From first item on, an AP Sylas kites and the Hijack threat keeps it level.
audit.corrected: Level 2 Sylas (3/10), Level 3 Sylas (3/10), Level 6 Cho'Gath (7/10), First item Skill, 2+ items Skill. Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three factual errors, all repeated across fields. (a) 'ignores his shields' appears three times — Sylas's kit contains no shield at all, and true damage is absorbed by shields anyway, so the claim would be wrong even if he had one. (b) Petricite Burst is called a heal ('his shields and Petricite Burst heal', 'his W (Kingslayer / Petricite Burst) heals the trade'). Petricite Burst is the passive: it stores a charge on every spell cast and expends it on the next basic attack for bonus magic damage plus attack speed. It heals nothing. The heal is Kingslayer (W). (c) Chain Lash is called a drain ('E1 plus Q drain') — it damages and slows, with a delayed explosion at the intersection, and has no healing.
audit.why: Riot text — Petricite Burst: 'After casting a spell, Sylas stores a charge... expend a charge and whirl his energized chains around him dealing bonus magic damage... he gains attack speed.' Kingslayer: 'Sylas lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions', 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s, 400 range. Chain Lash: 10/9/8/7/6s, 775 range, slow plus delayed explosion. Abscond/Abduct: 13/12/11/10/9s, 400 range — 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — the recast pulls him TO an enemy, so his exit depends on there being a minion behind him. Hijack: 80/55/30s, 950 range — at rank 3 it is back up every 30 seconds.
audit.corrected: Kingslayer named as the heal and the shield claim removed in spikes[1].text, whys[4], wants.you[2], early and report[5].t; the Abduct chain-pull mechanic and the minion-behind-him tell added to dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; Hijack's 30s rank-3 cooldown added to spikes[1].text and its 80s rank-1 to phases[4].why.

edits.before: Sylas owns levels 2-3 here. He opens with E1 to close, drops his Q (Chain Lash) for the burn zone, and recasts E2 to stun and dash back out — all while his W (Kingslayer / Petricite Burst) heals the trade. Your Rupture is a slow, telegraphed ground-pop, so throwing it on cooldown just feeds a champ who can E-dash sideways out of the ring. Last-hit off Carnivore, hold Feral Scream to silence his E-recast if he overcommits, and accept this window is his.
edits.after: Sylas owns levels 2-3 here. He opens with Abscond to close, drops Chain Lash for the burn zone, and recasts Abduct to chain himself back out through a minion — all while Kingslayer heals the trade and Petricite Burst adds free damage on his autos. Your Rupture is a slow, telegraphed ground-pop, so throwing it on cooldown just feeds a champ who can dash sideways out of the ring. Last-hit off Carnivore, hold Feral Scream for an overcommit, and accept this window is his.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left alone deliberately: the page calls the Abduct recast a stun in several places. Riot's Data Dragon text only says it throws chains and pulls Sylas to the enemy hit, and the kit carries no hardCC flag on E — but needsResearch is empty, which per the brief means UNKNOWN, not 'no'. I neither asserted nor removed the stun claim; every edit I made describes the recast by its verified behaviour (the chain-pull) instead. If the user can confirm Abduct applies a brief stun, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns could both carry it.
